about: LH035 included rows. Rows I01 to I40 are filled from the instrument's own pages fetched on 2026-11-02 with WebFetch (which returns a model-written extract of the page, not the raw page); rows I41 to I48 from raw curl reads of 2026-11-05 saved in data/reads-2026-11-05/, except where 'how_read' names a 2 November extract. Rows I01 to I40 were re-read raw on 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/), except I30, whose pages refused the research client; fields the raw pages did not bear out were corrected in version 0.3. Each row's 'date_read' and 'how_read' say which; 'not stated' means the pages read did not give it. 'blind_spot' is Lighthouse's reading (interpretation), not the instrument's statement. 'literature' cites papers opened in this run (literature.json). 'origin': a = used by Lighthouse's studies, b = an LH003 row, c = the fixed search plan (search ids as in searchlog.md).

rows.name: PeeringDB
rows.origin: c (named in the summary of search L1b; documentation read directly)
rows.counts: Records of networks, facilities, exchanges and carriers: a record "can be a carrier, a facility, an exchange, or a network"
rows.vantage: Self-reported: users affiliate with organisations, approved by admins or PeeringDB Support; network and organisation records can be prefilled by RDAP lookups
rows.cadence: not stated (the FAQ says only that its sync tool's later runs "incrementally update changed records")
rows.access: "freely available"; "no membership fees"; API access now needs an API key (because of mandatory MFA); licence not stated
rows.cannot_see: not stated on the page read
rows.blind_spot: Only what operators choose to declare: a declared presence at a facility or exchange, not whether traffic flows there or at what volume.
rows.literature: Sermpezis et al. 2023 (L05) note as a limitation of their own inputs that "only 25% of ASNs have records in PeeringDB".
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: TeleGeography Submarine Cable Map
rows.origin: c (TeleGeography named in the summary of search L1b; documentation read directly)
rows.counts: Submarine cable systems with length in kilometres and ready-for-service date; the FAQ gives "more than 600 active and planned submarine cables" and "over 1.5 million kilometers" in service (as of 2026)
rows.vantage: Operators' own accounts, for the paid research service's capacity figures: "We directly contact cable operators worldwide to obtain their current views on each system's capabilities"; also updates sent by the public; fault figures from the ICPC
rows.cadence: "We continually update this free resource"; capacity metrics "annually"
rows.history: not stated for the map; the fault dashboard covers "publicly-disclosed faults on subsea cables since 2017"
rows.access: The map is a "free resource"; raw geocoded data needs "an annual license"; capacity data "only available as part of our subscription-based research services"; map images CC BY-SA 4.0
rows.page_date: not stated; counts given "As of 2026" and "As of early 2026"
rows.cannot_see: "The cable routes on our map are stylized and do not reflect the precise geolocation of systems." Capacity is not in the free map.
rows.blind_spot: Land networks and what the cables carry: it is a register of systems as their owners describe them, with capacity behind a subscription.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: Epoch AI, AI data centers
urls_read: https://epoch.ai/data/data-centers (the extract names the page epoch.ai/data/ai-data-centers)
rows.origin: b (LH003's Epoch AI row; included under the brief's exception for AI-subject sources that observe a layer)
rows.counts: 96 AI data centres, each with "a timeline of total IT power capacity, compute capacity, and capital cost", location, owner and users
rows.vantage: Estimates from "high-resolution satellite imagery, permits, and public documents" and company statements; compute derived from power
rows.cadence: files marked "Updated Nov. 1, 2026" when read on 2 November and "Updated Nov. 5, 2026" on 6 November; schedule not stated
rows.history: timeline axis Q1 2023 to Q1 2030 (later quarters are projections); coverage limited "to data centers that become operational in 2024 or later, with some exceptions"
rows.access: free CSV and ZIP; "free to use, distribute, and reproduce provided the source and authors are credited" (CC BY)
rows.page_date: updated 1 November 2026 (2 November read); "Updated Nov. 5, 2026" (6 November read)
rows.cannot_see: "we estimate this database's coverage of global deployed AI computing capacity to be 45%" (90% interval 30% to 78%); power estimates within a factor of 1.4 "80% of the time"; "we are uncertain about these affiliations, especially the data center users"; coverage being expanded in "Asia, Europe and the Middle East"
rows.blind_spot: Every data centre that is not built for AI, and most of the internet's ordinary facilities.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: Interconnection Measurement Project (CableLabs)
rows.origin: c (search L1a results 5 and 7 named it; the result's site opened at its root)
rows.counts: "the total amount of ingress data (in bytes) on each interconnect over a 5 minute period" and each interconnect's capacity; published as utilisation distributions and monthly peaks
rows.vantage: Four ISPs' own interconnects: Comcast, Charter, Cox and Mediacom, whose footprint "covers >75%" of the US population
rows.cadence: collected every 5 minutes; published as monthly peaks and yearly distributions
rows.access: aggregated, normalised charts on the page; whether raw data can be had is not stated
rows.cannot_see: "a 95% utilization does not necessarily indicate a poor user experience"; "the percentage of interconnects at the various utilization thresholds is not weighted by capacity"; "the largest interconnections for ISPs are typically application specific"
rows.blind_spot: Every network but four US cable ISPs, and any single link: only aggregates are public, and the period read ends in 2024.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: RouteViews
rows.origin: c (named in the summary of search L2b; page read directly)
rows.counts: BGP routing information bases (RIBs) and updates
rows.vantage: Route collectors at "Internet Exchange Points (IXPs) and partner networks worldwide", by direct or multi-hop peering; "over a thousand peers"
rows.cadence: no publication schedule stated; the page says the archive documents routing "second by second" and is "continuously growing", and offers "Real-time BGP Data Access"
rows.access: free download from archive.routeviews.org; CC BY 4.0; commercial terms for selling derivative products
rows.page_date: not stated (newest news item shown as "1 week ago" on 6 November 2026)
rows.cannot_see: not stated on the page read
rows.blind_spot: The routes of networks that do not peer with a collector, which the literature puts at most networks.
rows.literature: Alfroy et al. 2024 (L06): "A tiny fraction (1.3%) of the 74k ASes" host a RIS or RouteViews vantage point; a private collector (bgp.tools) saw 192k AS links no RIS or RouteViews point saw. Sermpezis et al. 2023 (L05): average bias score 0.15 for RouteViews, against 0.00 to 0.01 for a random sample.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: RIPE RIS (Routing Information Service)
rows.origin: c (named in the summaries of searches L2a and L4a; documentation read directly)
rows.counts: BGP routing data in MRT files: "Dump files store the state of the routing system at a given time", and update files the changes
rows.vantage: BGP peering sessions with RIS: "We receive this data via BGP peering sessions, where RIPE RIS uses AS12654"; "Most route collectors collect data from peers at IXP peering LANs"; RRC00, RRC24 and RRC25 are multi-hop collectors
rows.cadence: "dumps are created every 8 hours, and updates are created every 5 minutes"
rows.history: not stated on the pages read
rows.access: raw data linked from data.ris.ripe.net; licence and terms not stated on the pages read
rows.page_date: route collectors page last updated 13 October 2026; MRT page 29 March 2024
rows.cannot_see: "Deprecated RRCs will not have new data but their data will be accessible." No coverage limit stated.
rows.blind_spot: As RouteViews: networks without a peering session, and a placement weighted towards exchange points.
rows.literature: Alfroy et al. 2024 (L06): RIS had 1,526 vantage points in May 2023, RouteViews 1,071; about 32% full feeders. Sermpezis et al. 2023 (L05): "RIPE RIS is heavily biased towards larger networks and IXPs" (average bias 0.16).
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: Packet Clearing House BGP routing data
rows.origin: c (search L2a result 6, opened)
rows.counts: not stated; the listing names "Daily Routing Snapshots" and "MRT Routing Updates"
rows.vantage: not stated on the page read
rows.cadence: not stated
rows.access: the page says "This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution ShareAlike 4.0 License" while its link points to CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
rows.cannot_see: not stated
rows.note: The page read is a directory listing. The search summary's figure of more than 225 exchange points was not on it and is not used.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: CAIDA AS Relationships
rows.origin: c (named in the summary of search L4a)
rows.counts: Inferred customer-to-provider and peer-to-peer links between ASes ("The AS relationships available are customer-provider (and provider-customer in the opposite direction), and peer-to-peer"; the page's background also describes sibling-to-sibling relationships, which that list does not include); customer cones in ASes, prefixes or addresses
rows.vantage: Derived from "RouteViews and RIPE RIS BGP table snapshots"; serial-2 adds IX looking-glass communities and Ark traceroutes
rows.cadence: "one file created per month"
rows.history: serial-1 "available from 1998 to present"; serial-2 from October 2015
rows.access: publicly available through a download or request form under CAIDA's Acceptable Use Agreement; publications must be reported
rows.cannot_see: "A truly accurate picture of the Internet topology would require collection of data from every AS"; "AS relationships are more complex than allowed for in our approach"
rows.blind_spot: Inherits the collectors' blind spots, since it is inferred from them.
rows.literature: Alfroy et al. 2024 (L06) report about 15% more AS relationships inferred when vantage points are chosen for low redundancy, at the same data volume.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: Cloudflare Radar
rows.origin: b (LH003 row) and c (search L10b result 16 is a variant of the page read)
rows.counts: Shares of HTTP requests, DNS queries to 1.1.1.1, domain rankings by "estimated number of unique users that access a domain", BGP messages and announced space in /24s and /48s, route leaks and hijacks, certificates in monitored CT logs, outages as an "algorithmically-observed anomalous drop in traffic", attacks in bytes or mitigated requests
rows.vantage: "Cloudflare's global network" and "aggregated and anonymized data from Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 public DNS resolver"; routing from "MRT data from RouteViews and RIPE RIS" plus RIS Live and RouteViews' Kafka stream; CT logs "currently monitored by Cloudflare"; speed tests run by users
rows.cadence: not stated overall; "the aggregation resolution for the ratio data is based on the length of the selected timeframe"
rows.history: not stated overall (speed tests "aggregated over the previous 90 days"; IPv6 share computed differently before 23 January 2023)
rows.access: "Available on all plans"; free API; API data under CC BY-NC 4.0
rows.cannot_see: "only countries where users run speed tests with sufficient regularity are included"; IQI gaps "do not indicate outages"; geolocation from "a third-party database" whose accuracy mobile networks, VPNs and proxies affect; robots.txt view: "we only include AI-focused user agents"
rows.blind_spot: Traffic that never touches Cloudflare's network or resolver; its routing view inherits the public collectors'.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: RIPE Atlas
rows.origin: c (named in the summaries of searches L3a and L3b; page read directly)
rows.counts: measurements of connectivity by "a global network of devices, called probes and anchors, that actively measure Internet connectivity"; unit not stated
rows.vantage: Volunteer-hosted probes ("over 14,000") and anchors
rows.cadence: not stated ("real time")
rows.access: "The vast majority of data that RIPE Atlas collects is freely available to anyone to browse, download or use"; custom measurements cost credits
rows.cannot_see: not stated on the page read
rows.blind_spot: Places where no volunteer hosts a probe.
rows.literature: Sermpezis et al. 2023 (L05): Atlas "substantially less biased" than RIS and RouteViews (average 0.06); its default probe selection is "almost two times higher" in bias than random selection.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: CAIDA Ark IPv4 Routed /24 Topology
rows.origin: c (named in the summary of search L4a)
rows.counts: traceroute path records in warts format (probe and response fields per hop)
rows.vantage: "a globally distributed set of Ark monitors"
rows.cadence: "a random address in each prefix is probed approximately every 24 hours"
rows.access: data older than one year public on request; recent data for academic researchers and US government agencies, companies through membership; CAIDA Acceptable Use Agreement
rows.cannot_see: "Measurements to consistent IPv4 addresses are not available in this dataset"; prefixes "are not probed by the same set of monitors consistently over time"
rows.blind_spot: IPv6 is outside this dataset by its definition; the newest year is not public.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: Censys (platform and the public PHP2Shell tracker)
rows.origin: a (LH033) and c (search L5b results 3, 7, 9, 10; L6b result 1)
rows.counts: hosts ("public IPv4 and IPv6 hosts"), web properties ("a hostname and a port"), certificates ("over 15 billion records"); the tracker counts "PHP responses Censys scanners receive per minute, by the version they report" and services per branch
rows.vantage: Censys's "internet scanning processes"; the tracker reads the version each PHP response reports
rows.cadence: certificates grow "daily"; the tracker is "Updated hourly"
rows.history: not stated in the documentation; plan history from "1+ month" (Core) to "12+ months" (Security Operations); the tracker shows the last 24 hours and one bar per UTC day
rows.access: free account for "basic visibility into standard ports and services" (limits not stated); paid plans "Contact sales"; the tracker's terms not stated
rows.cannot_see: not stated in the documentation read; the tracker's "Notes & limitations" heading had no text under it
rows.blind_spot: Services that do not answer its scanners or that report no version; a reported version is not a patch state.
rows.literature: Durumeric et al. 2025 (L01, Censys's own authors): Censys sees an estimated "98% of IPv4-based services on the top 10 ports, 97% of the top 100 ports, and 62% of services across all 65K ports"; "we do not conduct comprehensive IPv6 scans"; it restricts "data that is ripe for abuse". Bennett et al. 2021 (L02): Censys and Shodan made all planted test tokens visible within 24 hours, from five cloud machines.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: CAIDA UCSD Network Telescope
rows.origin: c (named in the summary of search L10b)
rows.counts: unsolicited one-way traffic (background radiation) to unused addresses; packets and "flowtuples"
rows.vantage: a routed but lightly used /9 and /10, "approximately 1/256th of all IPv4 addresses"
rows.cadence: "a continuous view"; exclusion filters updated twice daily since November 2023
rows.history: datasets back to Code Red (August 2001); aggregated flows from November 2003
rows.access: free for US and vetted foreign academic researchers; paying industry partners; sensitive data only on a VM platform; "Several historical datasets are available for download, either publicly or upon request"
rows.cannot_see: "System resource limitations sometimes cause packets to be dropped, or failure to generate flowtuples"; "The telescope instrumentation is in need of an overhaul to keep up with traffic growth"
rows.blind_spot: Traffic aimed at addresses that are in use, and scanners that avoid dark space.
rows.literature: Degen et al. 2026 (L09): after excluding assigned subnets the UCSD telescope monitors 10.9 million addresses; larger telescopes "detect many attacks missed by smaller ones"; 37.0% of sources targeted a /16 block in each of three telescopes within an hour.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: Tranco
rows.origin: c (named in the summary of search L7a)
rows.counts: domains ranked by averaging ranks "over the past 30 days"
rows.vantage: combines provider lists: CrUX, Cloudflare Radar, Farsight, Majestic and Cisco Umbrella (the page also says "all four providers", an inconsistency on the page)
rows.cadence: not stated for Tranco; sources daily (Farsight, Majestic, Umbrella), weekly (Radar) and monthly (CrUX)
rows.access: download section and source code offered; licence not stated
rows.page_date: not stated (content refers to mid-2023 events)
rows.cannot_see: inherited per source: Majestic "only domains linked to from other websites are considered"; Umbrella "invalid domains are also included"; CrUX "Only websites are included."
rows.blind_spot: Popularity, not existence: names nobody visits, links or resolves through the panels are absent.
rows.literature: Le Pochat et al. 2019 (L03): the four source lists then held about 2.82 million sites and agreed on about 70,000; all were manipulated in experiments; Tranco inherits their biases and lists "remain susceptible to manipulation" if all four are manipulated.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: Chrome UX Report (CrUX)
rows.origin: c (named in the summary of search L7b as HTTP Archive's URL source)
rows.counts: "individual user experiences, which are aggregated into page-level and origin-level distributions"
rows.vantage: Chrome users with usage-statistics reporting on, history sync on and no sync passphrase, on desktop and Android; not "Chrome on iOS", WebView apps or other Chromium browsers
rows.cadence: not stated on the page read
rows.access: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0
rows.cannot_see: the popularity threshold "is not disclosed"; pages must be "publicly discoverable"; "Chrome does not publish data about the proportions of users that meet these criteria"
rows.blind_spot: Sites below an undisclosed popularity floor and people on other browsers.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: Certificate Transparency logs
rows.origin: c (search L5b result 6, an encyclopaedia page, not opened; the project's documentation read directly)
rows.counts: certificates and precertificates in "append-only ledgers of certificates"
rows.vantage: "Anyone can submit a certificate to a log, but most of them are submitted by CAs"
rows.cadence: maximum merge delay "usually 24 hours"
rows.access: "anyone can query them"
rows.cannot_see: not stated on the page read
rows.blind_spot: Names that never receive a publicly trusted certificate.
rows.literature: Sommese et al. 2023 (L07, preprint): CT logs from 2017 covered 52% of the names in 19 ccTLD zones in 2023; "Scraping CT logs does not provide an explicit and reliable indicator of the publication time of a certificate". Gustafsson et al. 2017 (L11): for almost all domains seen on a campus network to December 2015 at least one log held a valid DV certificate, when logging was still voluntary for most CAs.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: The Shadowserver Foundation
rows.origin: c (search L5b result 13 not opened; named in the summary of search L9b)
rows.counts: remediation reports per exposure type: hosts with an accessible service, sinkholed connections, honeypot events; units vary by report
rows.vantage: "daily Internet-wide scans, sinkholes, honeypot sensors, sandboxes, blocklists and many other sources"
rows.cadence: most reports "Updated every 24 hours"
rows.access: "offers all services free of charge, for public benefit. We don't sell data"; reports go to vetted subscribers ("more than 10000" on one page, "over 8,000" on the other); a public dashboard is linked but could not be read
rows.cannot_see: no general statement; the DDoS report notes "traffic might also be spoofed"
rows.blind_spot: A reader who is not a network owner sees only what the dashboard aggregates; the reports go to those who can fix things.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: urlscan.io
rows.origin: c (search L5b result 4 not opened; about page read directly)
rows.counts: scans: a browser visit to a submitted URL, recording "everything that the page navigation creates"; "3M user-submitted scans per day"
rows.vantage: submissions from "researchers, analysts and automated pipelines"; scanning location not stated
rows.cadence: not stated as a schedule; "3M user-submitted scans per day"
rows.access: "a free service"; commercial API plans "alongside the free tier"
rows.page_date: a footer stamp that changes with each fetch (2 November 2026 on the first read, 6 November on the second)
rows.cannot_see: "A single observation is often meaningless without the necessary context."
rows.blind_spot: Only what someone thought worth submitting, which leans towards the suspicious.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: HTTP Archive
rows.origin: c (search L7b result 2 not opened; FAQ read directly)
rows.counts: one landing page per URL, "millions of URLs" per crawl; technologies by Wappalyzer ("over 1,000 web technologies")
rows.vantage: a private WebPageTest instance in "Google Cloud regions" in the US; URLs from the Chrome UX Report; desktop Chrome and emulated Android
rows.cadence: monthly, on "the 2nd Tuesday of each month"
rows.history: project started "in 2010"; first crawl date not stated
rows.access: public BigQuery dataset; cost and licence not stated
rows.cannot_see: "does not crawl the website's other pages"; "The landing page may not be representative of the overall site"; "Each URL is loaded only once"; tests "generated from various datacenters in the US"
rows.blind_spot: Internal and logged-in pages, and the web as seen from outside the US.
rows.literature: Aqeel et al. 2020 (L08): internal pages of 1,000 sites "differ substantially" from landing pages, and nearly two thirds of 119 web-performance studies would need revision to apply to them; their own sample is the top 2,000 or so sites.
rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: W3Techs
rows.origin: a (LH033); LH003 excluded it as not AI-specific
rows.counts: technology usage per website, across "well over 20 million sites"
rows.vantage: a sample of "the relevant web", ranked by CrUX and a customised Tranco list; crawler location not stated
rows.cadence: "Our reports are updated daily."
rows.access: statistics shown on the pages; terms of use and an API linked; payment not stated
rows.cannot_see: "We investigate technologies of websites, not of individual web pages"; "We do not consider subdomains to be separate websites"; "our research does not cover all technologies"; "Some technologies may become visible only after user interaction"; results "may be incomplete and inaccurate"

rows.how_read: WebFetch extract, 2 November 2026; raw re-read 6 November 2026 (data/reads-2026-11-06/)

rows.name: Common Crawl
rows.origin: b (LH003 row) and c (named in the summary of search L7a)
rows.counts: "raw web page data, metadata extracts, and text extracts"; "petabytes of data"
rows.vantage: CCBot ("Nutch-based"), from dedicated IP ranges listed as of 11 August 2026; obeys robots.txt and nofollow
rows.cadence: not stated on the pages read (crawls listed from CC-MAIN-2016-40 to CC-MAIN-2026-43)
